text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Information, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Joyce Mujuru this week admitted that there were flaws in the awarding of a licence to operate the country's second cellular phone network to Telecel Zimbabwe, and said all submitted tenders should be revaluated.

- The government is to freeze new applications for payouts from the War Victims Compensation Fund from September and has given individuals who illegally siphoned millions of dollars from the fund three months to repay the money or face prosecution, sources said.

- The Public Service Association, Zimbabwe's largest civil servants' body, has given the government until the end of June to report on progress towards the harmonisation of labour laws governing private and public sector employees.

- Zimbabwe's cabinet is expected to approve soon the commercialisation of the District Development Fund's aircraft section, to allow it to operate local and regional charter flights under the name Falcon Air.
- An occupational health and safety management expert has called for a nationwide inquiry into the flagrant flouting of rules and regulations by local companies.

- Zimbabwe's Information, Posts and Telecommunications Minister Joyce Mujuru said she would not contest a court order which set aside the award of the country's second cellular phone network licence to the Telecel firm.
- The 33rd heads of state and government assembly of the Organisation of African Unity ended in Harare on Wednesday.
